Most rows are unallocated (no project/instance), created in a bulk import in July 2012; a small fraction were later associated with projects and instances (2012-2013).

col_001.name: created_at
col_001.description: Row creation timestamp. All rows fall within a few minutes on 2012-07-05, indicating a bulk creation/import of the floating IP pool.

col_002.name: updated_at
col_002.description: Last update timestamp; null for rows never modified since creation (97.9%). Non-null values (2012-09 to 2013-08) correspond to IPs that were allocated/associated at some point.

col_003.name: deleted_at
col_003.description: Soft-delete timestamp; entirely null in this dump, so no floating IP rows were deleted.

col_004.name: id
col_004.description: Primary key / unique row identifier (1..8190, all distinct).

col_005.name: address
col_005.description: The floating IP address in CIDR notation, e.g. '10.0.10.172/8'. All unique, all in the 10.x.x.x private range.

col_006.name: fixed_ip_id
col_006.description: Reference to the fixed_ips table (the fixed IP the floating IP is mapped to). Entirely null here, so no floating IP is currently NATed to a fixed IP in this dump.

col_007.name: project_id
col_007.description: UUID of the OpenStack project/tenant that has allocated the floating IP; null for unallocated IPs. The 24 distinct UUIDs match the ~2% of rows with an update timestamp.

col_009.name: auto_assigned
col_009.description: Boolean flag (TINYINT) indicating whether the IP was auto-assigned; always 0 (false) in this dump.

col_010.name: pool
col_010.description: Name of the floating IP pool the address belongs to; constant value 'nova' (the default pool) for all rows.

col_011.name: interface
col_011.description: Network interface on which the floating IP is served; constant 'eth0' for all rows.

col_012.name: deleted
col_012.description: Soft-delete flag; always 0 (not deleted), consistent with deleted_at being entirely null.

table.name: instance_actions
table.purpose: OpenStack Nova audit log of actions performed on instances (create, delete, reboot, live-migration, stop, etc.), one row per action, with the acting user/project and request ID. Detailed per-event traces live in instance_actions_events, which references this table's id.

col_001.name: created_at
col_001.description: Timestamp when the action record was created (row insertion time).

col_002.name: updated_at
col_002.description: Timestamp when the action record was last updated; null for actions never updated after creation.

col_003.name: deleted_at
col_003.description: Soft-delete timestamp; always null here (no rows soft-deleted). The table appears to have two columns with this role (see the other deleted_at column), so which one is the canonical Nova deleted_at is ambiguous; both are null in all rows.

col_004.name: id
col_004.description: Auto-increment primary key of the action record; unique across all rows and referenced by instance_actions_events.

col_005.name: action
col_005.description: Name of the instance action performed, e.g. create, delete, reboot, live-migration, stop, resize, changePassword, unrescue, migrate.

col_006.name: instance_uuid
col_006.description: UUID of the instance the action was performed on; references instances.

col_007.name: request_id
col_007.description: API request ID (req-<uuid>) that triggered the action; groups multiple actions from one API call.

col_008.name: user_id
col_008.description: UUID/hex ID of the user who initiated the action; null for system-initiated actions.

col_009.name: project_id
col_009.description: UUID/hex ID of the project (tenant) owning the instance; null for system-initiated actions.

col_010.name: start_time
col_010.description: Timestamp when the action started (slightly before or equal to created_at).

col_011.name: deleted_at
col_011.description: Second soft-delete timestamp column (Nova schema normally has deleted_at plus a deleted flag); always null here. Ambiguous: the table has two deleted_at-like columns and no join evidence distinguishes them, so this could alternatively be a duplicate/archived copy artifact.

col_012.name: message
col_012.description: Error message for failed actions; only value observed is 'Error', null for successful actions.

col_013.name: deleted
col_013.description: Soft-delete flag; 0 = not deleted (all rows are 0).

table.name: instance_actions_events
table.purpose: OpenStack Nova table recording individual trace events for each instance action (e.g. each compute step within a build, reboot, resize, terminate). Each row is one event belonging to an action in instance_actions, with start/finish times and outcome. The shadow_ prefix tables are archived copies of the same schema.

col_001.name: created_at
col_001.description: Timestamp when the event row was created (row creation time, not necessarily the event's logical start).

col_002.name: updated_at
col_002.description: Timestamp when the event row was last updated; null when the row was never updated after creation.

col_003.name: deleted_at
col_003.description: Soft-delete timestamp; 100% null here, so no rows are soft-deleted.

col_004.name: id
col_004.description: Auto-increment primary key of the event row (unique across all rows). The detected joins to shadow_reservations are coincidental numeric overlaps, not real relationships.

col_005.name: event
col_005.description: Name of the event/step within the action, e.g. compute__do_build_and_run_instance, compute_terminate_instance, compute_reboot_instance, compute_prep_resize, schedule. These are Nova compute-task trace event names.

col_006.name: action_id
col_006.description: Foreign key to instance_actions.id; multiple events belong to one action (many_to_one).

col_007.name: start_time
col_007.description: When the event started; values mirror created_at (Nova sets both at event start).

col_008.name: finish_time
col_008.description: When the event finished; null while the event is still running or was never finished.

col_009.name: result
col_009.description: Outcome of the event: 'Success' or 'Error'; null when the event has not finished.

col_010.name: traceback
col_010.description: Python traceback text recorded when the event failed; 97% null because most events succeed. Values are hex-like strings, likely md5 hashes of traceback content (Nova stores a hash of the traceback).

col_011.name: deleted
col_011.description: Soft-delete flag; always 0, no rows deleted.

col_012.name: host
col_012.description: Unresolved: 100% null VARCHAR. In Nova's schema this position is 'host' (compute host that executed the event), but no values exist to confirm.

col_013.name: details
col_013.description: Unresolved: 100% null VARCHAR. In Nova's schema this position is 'details' (event detail payload), but no values exist to confirm.

table.name: instance_extra
table.purpose: OpenStack Nova 'instance_extra' table: one row per instance holding rarely-read, bulky or optional instance attributes (NUMA topology, PCI requests, flavor snapshot, vCPU model, migration context, cell mapping) kept separate from the main 'instances' table. The database is a Nova cloud controller database (with shadow_* archival copies).

col_001.name: created_at
col_001.description: Row creation timestamp (Nova standard audit column).

col_002.name: updated_at
col_002.description: Row last-update timestamp (Nova standard audit column).

col_003.name: deleted_at
col_003.description: Soft-delete timestamp; null for ~79% of rows, i.e. rows not deleted.

col_004.name: deleted
col_004.description: Soft-delete flag (Nova convention: 0 = live, nonzero id = deleted, set to the deleting row's id). The 1512 rows with value 0 are live; other values are ids of deleted rows.

col_005.name: id
col_005.description: Primary key of instance_extra; unique integer, one-to-one with shadow_instances.col_004 (the instance id).

col_006.name: instance_uuid
col_006.description: UUID of the instance this extra data belongs to; joins to instances.uuid, instance_info_caches and instance_id_mappings.

col_007.name: cells
col_007.description: Serialized Nova object (nova_object version 1.2) recording the cell(s) the instance was mapped to; populated only in cells deployments (99% null here).

col_008.name: pci_requests
col_008.description: Serialized PCI device requests for the instance (e.g. GPU alias requests with count and vendor/product spec); '[]' when no PCI devices were requested.

col_009.name: flavor
col_009.description: Serialized Flavor object snapshot with 'new'/'old'/'cur' variants, used during resize to track current, old and new flavors of the instance.

col_010.name: vcpu_model
col_010.description: Serialized VCPUModel object (fields vendor, features, model...) describing the virtual CPU model exposed to the guest.

col_011.name: migration_context
col_011.description: Serialized Nova MigrationContext object (its data includes the instance_uuid and migration-time fields such as source/destination details), stored on the instance_extra row while a resize or live-migration is in progress; null for the ~97% of instances with no migration underway.

table.name: instance_faults
table.purpose: OpenStack Nova-style record of faults/errors that occurred on virtual server instances: one row per fault event, with HTTP-like error code, message, details, host, and soft-delete metadata. (A shadow_instance_faults table also exists, consistent with Nova's archiving scheme.)

col_001.name: created_at
col_001.description: Timestamp when the fault record was created.

col_002.name: updated_at
col_002.description: Timestamp of last update to the row; never populated in this data (100% null). Plausible alternative: a standard Nova audit column that is simply unused for fault records, which are typically written once and never updated.

col_003.name: deleted_at
col_003.description: Timestamp when the fault record was soft-deleted; null for ~75% of rows that are still live. The very high top-value counts (e.g. 1010 rows at one second) suggest bulk cleanup/archiving runs.

col_004.name: id
col_004.description: Auto-incrementing primary key of the fault record (unique across all rows).

col_005.name: instance_uuid
col_005.description: UUID of the instance (VM) the fault occurred on; references instances/instance_info_caches/instance_id_mappings. Repeated values mean one instance can have multiple fault records.

col_006.name: code
col_006.description: Fault/error code; values 400, 404, 500 mirror HTTP status codes (client error, not found, internal server error). 500 dominates.

col_007.name: message
col_007.description: Short error message for the fault. Values are 32-char hex strings, so the text appears hashed/anonymized in this dump; the underlying column is the fault message. Alternative reading: the column could store a message hash/digest natively, but Nova's schema defines it as the fault message text.

col_008.name: details
col_008.description: Longer error details/traceback, optional (~30% null). Values are 32-char hex strings, i.e. hashed/anonymized like the message column. Alternative reading: could be a hash of the details rather than the details themselves, but Nova's schema defines it as free-text details.

col_009.name: host
col_009.description: Hostname of the compute node where the fault occurred (e.g. spark9-96, shine-94).

col_010.name: deleted
col_010.description: Soft-delete marker: 0 for live rows; for deleted rows it holds the row's id (Nova's deleted=id convention), matching the non-null deleted_at timestamps.

table.name: instance_group_member
table.purpose: OpenStack Nova server-group membership table: each row links one instance (VM) to one server group (instance group).

col_001.name: created_at
col_001.description: Row creation timestamp.

col_002.name: updated_at
col_002.description: Last-update timestamp for the membership row; entirely null in this dump, so no rows were ever updated after creation. Alternative reading: the column may simply be unused in this deployment rather than never updated.

col_003.name: deleted_at
col_003.description: Timestamp when the membership row was soft-deleted; null for ~98.6% of rows (active memberships).

col_004.name: deleted
col_004.description: Soft-delete flag: 0 = active, nonzero (typically 1) = deleted. The 56 rows with value 0 correspond to active memberships; other values are the id of the deleted row in Nova's soft-delete convention.

col_005.name: id
col_005.description: Auto-increment primary key of the membership row (unique across all 4085 rows).

col_006.name: instance_uuid
col_006.description: UUID of the instance (VM) that is a member of the group; one-to-one with instance_id_mappings.

col_007.name: group_id
col_007.description: Foreign key to instance_groups.id — the server group the instance belongs to. 210 distinct groups, some with hundreds of members.

table.name: instance_group_policy
table.purpose: OpenStack Nova server-group policy table: one row per policy attached to an instance group (server group), specifying the scheduling policy (affinity or anti-affinity).

col_001.name: created_at
col_001.description: Row creation timestamp.

col_002.name: updated_at
col_002.description: Row last-update timestamp; entirely null in this dump (rows are never updated).

col_003.name: deleted_at
col_003.description: Soft-delete timestamp; null for ~88% of rows means the row is still live. Non-null values are later than created_at, consistent with deletion time.

col_004.name: group_id
col_004.description: Foreign key to instance_groups (the server group this policy applies to). Value 0 appears 28 times, likely a legacy/default group id.

col_005.name: id
col_005.description: Surrogate primary key of the policy row (unique across all 228 rows).

col_006.name: policy
col_006.description: Scheduling policy of the server group: 'anti-affinity' (spread instances across hosts) or 'affinity' (place on the same host).

col_007.name: id
col_007.description: Duplicate of the primary key id (col_005); identical values in every sampled row, likely a second id column from a schema migration. Join evidence shows instance_group_member.group_id referencing this column, which could alternatively mean it serves as the group identifier that memberships point at; which reading is canonical remains unresolved.

table.name: instance_groups
table.purpose: OpenStack Nova server groups: named groups of instances (VMs) with placement/anti-affinity policies, owned by a user and project. Policies and memberships live in instance_group_policy and instance_group_member, which reference this table's id. Rows are soft-deleted (deleted/deleted_at).

col_001.name: created_at
col_001.description: Timestamp when the server group row was created.

col_002.name: deleted_at
col_002.description: Timestamp when the row was soft-deleted; null for all rows (no deletions recorded, though 28 rows have deleted set).

col_003.name: updated_at
col_003.description: Timestamp of the last update to the group; ~12% null (never updated).

col_004.name: deleted
col_004.description: Soft-delete marker (Nova style): 0 for live rows; on deletion set to the row's id. 28 rows are deleted (non-zero values matching ids).

col_005.name: id
col_005.description: Primary key, auto-increment integer id of the server group. Referenced by instance_group_member, instance_group_policy, instances, migrations, pci_devices etc.

col_006.name: user_id
col_006.description: UUID-style hex id of the owning user; only 7 distinct users, one dominant.

col_007.name: project_id
col_007.description: UUID-style hex id of the owning project/tenant; 7 distinct projects.

col_008.name: uuid
col_008.description: Unique UUID of the server group (external API identifier).

col_009.name: name
col_009.description: Human-readable group name, unique per project (36 distinct synthetic names like 'helio-glint4').

table.name: instance_id_mappings
table.purpose: OpenStack Nova instance_id_mappings table: maps an instance's integer ID to its UUID, allowing lookups of instances by UUID without a UUID index on the main instances table. Each row is one instance ID/UUID pair. (The shadow_ prefixed tables indicate this is a Nova database with archived shadow copies.)

col_001.name: created_at
col_001.description: Timestamp when this ID mapping row was created.

col_002.name: updated_at
col_002.description: Timestamp when the row was last updated. Plausible reading: standard Nova audit column set alongside created_at/deleted_at; alternative reading is that it is only set on specific row modifications, which would explain it being always NULL in this data.

col_003.name: deleted_at
col_003.description: Timestamp when the row was soft-deleted (paired with the deleted flag, col_006). Plausible reading: standard Nova soft-delete timestamp; alternative reading is a generic archival timestamp, which would also fit the shadow-table archiving scheme present in this database. Always NULL here, consistent with no rows being soft-deleted.

col_004.name: id
col_004.description: Auto-increment integer primary key of the mapping row (unique across all rows).

col_005.name: uuid
col_005.description: Instance UUID; joins one-to-one to instances.uuid and is referenced by many instance-related tables (instance_actions, instance_metadata, block_device_mapping, migrations, etc.).

col_006.name: deleted
col_006.description: Soft-delete flag; 0 = not deleted. Constant 0 in this data.

table.name: instance_info_caches
table.purpose: OpenStack Nova table caching each instance's network information (VIFs, OVS interface IDs, IPs) keyed by instance UUID, with soft-delete columns. One row per instance.

col_001.name: created_at

col_002.name: updated_at
col_002.description: Last update timestamp; slightly nullable, always >= created_at.

col_003.name: deleted_at
col_003.description: Soft-delete timestamp; null for ~80% of rows means not deleted.

col_004.name: id
col_004.description: Auto-increment primary key of the cache row (unique integer).

col_005.name: network_info
col_005.description: JSON array of network interface (VIF) details for the instance: profile, ovs_interfaceid, prescriptive fields (mac, IPs, network). '[]' means no cached network info.

col_006.name: instance_uuid
col_006.description: UUID of the instance this network cache belongs to; one-to-one with instances.uuid and referenced by many instance-related tables.

col_007.name: deleted
col_007.description: Soft-delete flag: 0 = active, otherwise mirrors the instance's numeric id at deletion time (Nova convention of storing deleted id).

table.name: instance_metadata
table.purpose: OpenStack Nova instance metadata table: arbitrary key/value tags attached to a VM instance (instance_uuid). One row per metadata key per instance. This is the Nova database schema (instances, instance_info_caches, etc.).

col_001.name: created_at
col_001.description: Row creation timestamp.

col_002.name: updated_at
col_002.description: Row last-update timestamp; almost always null (rows never updated).

col_003.name: deleted_at

col_008.name: deleted

table.name: instance_system_metadata
table.purpose: OpenStack Nova instance system metadata: key/value pairs stored per instance (e.g. image properties, flavor attributes, injected passwords). One row per (instance, key) pair. The shadow_ prefix tables are archived copies; this is the live table.

col_001.name: created_at
col_001.description: Row creation timestamp (Nova standard audit column).

col_002.name: updated_at
col_002.description: Row last-update timestamp; null for rows never updated (Nova standard audit column).

col_003.name: deleted_at
col_003.description: Soft-delete timestamp; null for live rows (Nova standard audit column).

col_004.name: id
col_004.description: Auto-increment primary key of the metadata row (unique across all rows).

col_006.name: key
col_006.description: Metadata key name, e.g. image_min_disk, image_min_ram, image_base_image_ref, image_container_format, clean_attempts, password_N, image_instance_type_rxtx_factor.

col_007.description: Value for the metadata key; free-form text (e.g. flavor/image names like 'neon', 'spire_pulse', 'glint-shine', or image refs). Null when the key has no value.

col_008.name: deleted
col_008.description: Soft-delete flag: 0 = live row; non-zero values (matching an id) mark the deleted-by marker in Nova's soft-delete convention.

table.name: instance_types
